synthesis: The pointwise argument first uses RH to make the zero sum nonnegative and chooses the horizontal shift so its residual coefficient is nonpositive, leaving a smoothed von Mangoldt upper bound; the next unit then decomposes the nonprime terms, bounding powers of exponent at least three by O(1) and prime squares by O(log log log T), so the usable bound is reduced to primes at that error scale.
source_support: Unit u03 defines the nonnegative zero sum, integrates the logarithmic derivative, inserts the smoothed explicit formula, and chooses sigma_0 so the zero term in (7) may be omitted. Unit u04 explicitly invokes that main proposition and proves the subsequent restriction from prime powers to primes by separate estimates for exponents at least three and for squares.
nonparaphrase_operation: Composes two distinct eliminations in the proof pipeline: sign-engineering removes the zero contribution from a one-sided inequality, then exponent-wise estimates remove nonprime prime powers from the remaining arithmetic sum.
limits: The mechanism is RH-conditional and one-sided; it gives neither a lower bound nor an unconditional approximation of log zeta. Exact kernels, constants, and the shift threshold remain formula/OCR-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because neither parent alone yields the prime-only upper-bound mechanism: u03 supplies the zero-sign reduction to a prime-power polynomial, while u04 supplies the separate prime-power reduction.

synthesis: The high-moment lemma converts a short prime Dirichlet polynomial into factorially weighted diagonal data under the capacity constraint x^k <= T/log T. The theorem then chooses the cutoff and splits the polynomial into small- and large-prime pieces, forces one piece to be large, and assigns each piece an admissible moment order suited to its variance and length, producing the quadratic moderate-tail and V log V extreme-tail bounds.
source_support: Unit u05 expands the 2k-th moment, separates equal-product diagonals from oscillatory off-diagonals, uses x^k <= T/log T to subordinate the latter, and bounds the diagonal by k! times the coefficient square-sum. Unit u06 defines x and z, forms S1 and S2, proves the forced alternative for a large zeta value, and applies u05 with different allowed k choices to derive estimates (8) and (9).
nonparaphrase_operation: Links the abstract moment lemma's length budget to the regime-dependent cutoff and moment choices, explaining why distinct prime scales receive distinct probabilistic certificates and tail shapes.
limits: The conclusion is an RH-conditional upper-tail mechanism, not a limiting Gaussian law or a sharp asymptotic. The admissible ranges, constants, and displayed exponents are formula-dense and OCR-sensitive, and the length constraint contributes to the regime tuning and nonoptimal constants.
quality_reason: Accepted because u05 alone gives only a capacity-limited moment estimate and u06 alone relies on that estimate; together they support the concrete conversion from multiplicative diagonal combinatorics to scale-dependent tail bounds.

synthesis: Changing the averaging family changes the center while retaining a comparable log-log fluctuation scale: the unitary family has predicted center zero and moment exponent k^2, quadratic characters acquire a positive half-log-log contribution from prime squares and exponent k(k+1)/2, while elliptic quadratic twists acquire the opposite square-term shift and exponent k(k-1)/2. The family comparison therefore traces the exponent changes to arithmetic mean shifts rather than to variance alone.
source_support: Unit u07 gives the unitary k^2 upper-bound exponent and replaces time averaging by character orthogonality. Unit u08 identifies the positive prime-square shift and k(k+1)/2 exponent for quadratic characters; u09 identifies the negative square contribution and k(k-1)/2 exponent for elliptic twists. Unit u10 places the three cases together with predicted centers zero, positive, and negative and comparable log-log variances.
nonparaphrase_operation: Aligns local prime-square behavior, family-specific diagonalization, predicted centering, and global moment exponents across three families, isolating the sign of the surviving square term as the mechanism distinguishing the shifted cases.
limits: The proved frequency and moment statements are GRH-conditional upper bounds, whereas the Gaussian family laws are conjectural; exact moment asymptotics do not follow. The unitary zero center is stated as a distributional prediction rather than derived there from a prime-square calculation, elliptic twists require restriction to positive functional-equation sign, and a full Selberg-type law needs control of near-central zeros.
quality_reason: Accepted because the cross-unit comparison is concrete and source-supported: u08 and u09 supply opposite local square mechanisms and exponents, while u07 and u10 supply the unitary control and the common mean-variance frame unavailable from any one unit.
